Czech

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈpolɪ]
  • Rhymes: -olɪ
  • Hyphenation: po‧li

Noun

[edit]

poli

  1. inflection of pole:
    1. dative/locative singular
    2. instrumental plural

Anagrams

[edit]

Dutch

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Clipping of polikliniek.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpoː.li/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Hyphenation: po‧li
  • Rhymes: -oːli

Noun

[edit]

poli f (plural poli's, no diminutive)

  1. an outpatient clinic

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Indonesian: poli

Finnish

  • Syllabification(key): po‧li

Noun

[edit]

poli (colloquial)

  1. polyclinic

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin polītus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pɔ.li/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)

Adjective

[edit]

poli (feminine polie, masculine plural polis, feminine plural polies)

  1. polite
  2. polished

Related terms

[edit]
  • politesse
  • poliment

Noun

[edit]

poli m (plural polis)

  1. lustre, polish

Participle

[edit]

poli (feminine polie, masculine plural polis, feminine plural polies)

  1. past participle of polir

Related terms

[edit]
  • polir

Further reading

[edit]
  • “poli”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Anagrams

[edit]
  • poil

Indonesian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Dutch poli (“clinic, outpatient clinic”), from clipping of polikliniek.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Indonesian) IPA(key): /ˈpoli/ [ˈpo.li]
  • Rhymes: -oli
  • Syllabification: po‧li

Noun

[edit]

poli (plural poli-poli)

  1. (healthcare) clipping of poliklinik (“clinic, outpatient clinic”)
    Dokter dan perawat positif CoVID-19, poli rumah sakit ditutup. ― Doctor and nurse tested CoVID-19 positive, hospital outpatient clinic have been closed.

Italian

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

poli m pl

  1. plural of polo

Anagrams

[edit]

Latgalian

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

poli m pl

  1. flood

Latin

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

polī

  1. inflection of polus:
    1. nominative/vocative plural
    2. genitive singular

Latvian

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

poli m

  1. vocative/accusative/instrumental singular of polis

Lower Sorbian

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

poli

  1. superseded spelling of póli

Norman

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Latin poliō (“polish, smooth”).

Verb

[edit]

poli

  1. (Jersey) to polish

Etymology 2

[edit]

From Latin polītus (“polished, smoothed”), perfect passive participle of poliō (“polish, smooth”).

Verb

[edit]

poli

  1. past participle of poli

Adjective

[edit]

poli m

  1. (Jersey) polite
Derived terms
[edit]
  • polîment (“politely”)

Portuguese

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

poli

  1. inflection of polir:
    1. first-person singular preterite indicative
    2. second-person plural imperative

Serbo-Croatian

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

poli (Cyrillic spelling поли)

  1. second/third-person singular aorist past of politi

Slovak

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pɔʎi/, (high register) [ˈpɔʎi], (common) [ˈpɔli]
  • Rhymes: -ɔʎi
  • Hyphenation: po‧li

Noun

[edit]

poli n

  1. locative singular of pole

Spanish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpoli/ [ˈpo.li]
  • Rhymes: -oli
  • Syllabification: po‧li

Etymology 1

[edit]

Clipping of policía.

Noun

[edit]

poli m or f by sense (plural polis)

  1. (colloquial) cop
    Synonym: (Spain) madero

Noun

[edit]

poli f (uncountable)

  1. (colloquial) heat, the police
Derived terms
[edit]
  • poli bueno poli malo

Etymology 2

[edit]

Clipping of poliamoroso / borrowed from English poly.

Adjective

[edit]

poli m or f (masculine and feminine plural polis)

  1. (chiefly informal) polyamorous.

Further reading

[edit]
  • “poli”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025

West Makian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Cognate with Ternate fodi (“to buy”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpo.l̪i/

Verb

[edit]

poli

  1. (transitive) to buy

Conjugation

[edit]
Conjugation of poli (action verb)
singular plural
inclusive exclusive

2nd person nopoli fopoli

animate
